text: Highlight Clip: Star Xu: Hyperliquid's Matching Engine Is More Market Maker Friendly Star Xu: Hyperliquid's Matching Engine Is More Market Maker Friendly OKX founder Star Xu said on the New Era Finance Podcast that Hyperliquid differs fundamentally from centralized order book exchanges in its technical design. While centralized exchanges process orders individually, Hyperliquid matches orders block by block and prioritizes cancellations within each block, allowing market makers to cancel orders ahead of takers. He believes this market maker friendly design explains why Hyperliquid's order book depth appears better than that of many centralized exchanges, while offering another approach for long-tail assets with limited liquidity. — link

text: Liquid Network Keeps Bitcoin Redemptions Frozen, Reserve Gap About 603 BTC Liquid Network is running again, but peg-outs that convert L-BTC back to bitcoin remain suspended, with a reserve gap of about 603 BTC. Liquid said redemptions will not resume until reserves fully back all circulating L-BTC and security reviews are complete. A Sept. 6 Elements bug allowed unauthorized L-BTC creation and redemption. About 3,996 to 4,000 BTC left the federation reserve, then worth about $320 million. White-hat actors returned about 3,400 BTC on Sept. 7, leaving 598 to 603 BTC unreturned. As of Oct. 11, peg-outs remain paused. Blockstream CEO Adam Back said the 1:1 peg will ultimately be covered, with no date given. — link

text: XRPL fixes decade-old bug that could have minted trillions of XRP RippleX and the XRP Ledger Foundation disclosed that a critical payment-engine overflow bug could have allowed an attacker to create spendable XRP beyond the network's fixed supply using a specially crafted transaction. The issue, present in code dating back to 2015, was reported through the XRPL bug bounty program and fixed in xrpld 3.4.1 on September 25, with more than 80% of default validators upgraded that day. Security researcher @Cayden_Liao said his team's proof of concept could mint about 18 trillion XRP in a single transaction, roughly 184 times XRP's intended 100 billion supply, and earned the program's maximum $250,000 bounty. XRPL said it found no evidence the flaw was ever exploited on a public network. — link
